title: CheckboxGroup's helper and error text is described to a div, so nothing announces it
foundBy: writing the FormGroup development warning for CUI-090, which made the wiring visible in the DOM

evidence.verified:
`npm run ci` exits 0. All 733 existing tests pass alongside 9 new ones, the visual gate compared 112 of 112 captures at 0 differing pixels, and axe reports 0 violations with 0 rules matching more nodes. The `role="group"` added to CheckboxGroup changes no pixel.

Measured the same way the defect was found, by rendering and reading the DOM back. Before: `aria-describedby` on a `<div>` with no role for both Dropdown and CheckboxGroup, and `required` on `div,select` for a required Dropdown. After: `aria-describedby` on `<select>` for Dropdown and on `<div role="group">` for CheckboxGroup, and `required` on `select` alone.

The regression risk was the narrowed clone, since Input stopped being cloned and now reads context. Seven Input paths were rendered and read back: a generated id, an explicit htmlFor with an error, required forwarding, multiline, a consumer id winning over the generated one, a bare `<input>` child, and an Input outside any FormGroup. All wire as before, and the error border still follows `aria-invalid`.

The tests were proved able to fail by mutation. Restoring the old predicate, so that any element child is cloned again, failed 3 of the 9. Removing the provider failed 2. The file was restored and `git diff` read clean.

Measured on the artifact: `dist/index.d.ts` exports `useFormGroupField` and the `FormGroupField` type, `dist/index.js` carries the runtime export, `dist/components/Dropdown.js` carries `aria-describedby` and `dist/components/CheckboxGroup.js` carries `role: "group"`.

details:
`CheckboxGroup` wraps its own content in a `FormGroup`, passing `label`, `helper` and `error`, and hands it a single `<div>` as the child. `FormGroup` wires a child by cloning it, so the `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `required` it generates all land on that div.

Rendered and read back: the element carrying `aria-describedby="formgroup-<id>-helper"` is a `<div>` with no role, and the helper text it points at is on the page. `aria-describedby` on a non-interactive element with no role is not announced, so a reader using a screen reader is told neither the helper text nor, on an invalid group, the error. `aria-invalid` on the same div means nothing, and `required` does not survive onto it at all: a rendered group carrying `required` has zero elements with the attribute.

This is not the case CUI-090 was about. That record is about a contract reaching a consumer, and the warning written for it deliberately passes this: something does refer to the helper's id, so the wiring is present. It is pointed at an element that cannot carry it, which the warning's predicate does not test for and should not, because `FormGroup` cannot know what its child renders.

The fix belongs in `CheckboxGroup` rather than in `FormGroup`. A group of checkboxes has a natural home for this: a `role="group"` on the wrapper, or a `fieldset` with the label as its `legend`, either of which makes `aria-describedby` meaningful. Whichever is chosen also settles what `aria-invalid` should mean for a group.

notes.text: Worth checking the other composite that does this before fixing one of them. `Dropdown` also renders a `FormGroup` around its own content, and whether its child is the native `<select>` or a wrapper decides whether it has the same defect or none.

Dropdown had it too, which the note above asked someone to check. Its wrapper took the `aria-describedby` exactly as CheckboxGroup's did, and it also took `required`, which is not a valid attribute on a `<div>` at all. Its `<select>` already carried `required` and `aria-invalid` itself, so the clone was adding an invalid attribute and announcing nothing.

Labelling was never broken in Dropdown: it passes `htmlFor` and its wrapper already had its own id, so the label pointed at the select throughout, and no ids were duplicated.

Decided by the owner: FormGroup publishes the wiring rather than the two composites each working around it, and the stray `required` goes in the same change.

One deviation from the shape that was chosen, and the reason for it. The predicate is not "is this an intrinsic control" but "can this element carry the wiring": the native controls, plus an element already marked `role="group"` or `role="radiogroup"`. A set of checkboxes is a group and there is no single control for a label to name, so the group is where `aria-describedby` belongs, and CheckboxGroup declaring the role is what earns it the wiring. Restricting to native controls alone would have left CheckboxGroup with nowhere to put it.

Dropdown reads the ids rather than the context for its own group, because it renders that FormGroup and is therefore its parent: a hook there reads the enclosing group, not the one below. `fieldMessageIds` in `src/lib/formGroupField.ts` is the one derivation both use, so the two cannot drift. Dropdown reads the context as well, for the case where a consumer wraps it in a FormGroup of their own.

An attempt to extract Dropdown's control into a component under the provider was abandoned: it broke ref forwarding, because `forwardRefToRoot` needs the render to return a DOM element and a function component is not one. Two tests caught it.
